excerpts.text:
Today, the ethnic makeup of the New Zealand population is undergoing a process of change, with new waves of [immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_New_Zealand "Immigration to New Zealand"), higher birth rates and increasing [interracial marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interracial_marriage "Interracial marriage") resulting in the New Zealand population of Māori, [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_New_Zealanders "Asian New Zealanders"), [Pasifika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasifika_New_Zealanders "Pasifika New Zealanders") and [multiracial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial "Multiracial") descent growing at a higher rate than those of solely European descent, with such groups projected to make up a larger proportion of the population in the future.[[16]](#cite_note-17) New Zealand has an estimated resident population of around 5,324,700 (as of June 2025).[[17]](#cite_note-NZ_population_data_2018-18) Over one million New Zealanders recorded in the [2013 New Zealand census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_New_Zealand_census "2013 New Zealand census") were born overseas, and by 2021 over a quarter of New Zealanders are estimated to be foreign born.[[18]](#cite_note-19) Rapidly increasing ethnic groups vary from being well-established, such as [Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_New_Zealanders "Indian New Zealanders") and [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_New_Zealanders "Chinese New Zealanders"), to nascent ones such as [African New Zealanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_New_Zealanders "African New Zealanders").[[19]](#cite_note-20)

While most New Zealanders are resident in New Zealand, there is also a significant [diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diaspora "Diaspora"), estimated at around 750,000. Of these, about 640,800 lived in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") (a June 2013 estimate[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Zealanders&action=edit)),[[1]](#cite_note-Australia-1) which was equivalent to 12% of the resident population of New Zealand.
In addition, more than 120,000 Māori live in Australia.
